case_row.analysis_or_sense: chariots bought for five female jackals, Bhāṣya/Kāśikā price analysis

contrast.price_expression: pañcabhiḥ kroṣṭrībhiḥ, price stated with the feminine instrumental plural; PG230 already owns that position
contrast.context: rathaiḥ (chariots), masculine instrumental plural as head in the expanded phrase
contrast.price_adjective: pañcakroṣṭṛbhiḥ at a pause; inserted in this phrase as pañcakroṣṭṛbhī rathaiḥ. The length in bhī before r is external sandhi, not a new bhī case suffix.
contrast.male_control: bare kroṣṭubhiḥ from 7.1.97 belongs to the male-animal stem. It is not a substitute for the feminine full-price term.

two_derivations.feminine_condition: Kāśikā on 7.1.96: if listed in gaurādi, ṅīṣ is supplied and some take that affix as the condition for tṛj-like form. If not so listed, the female sense itself licenses tṛj-like form; then ṅīp follows under 4.1.5. The two cases do not demand distinct surface vowels.
two_derivations.price_luk: The Nyāsa identifies the taddhita-price compound (2.1.51), ṭhak in the relevant range (5.1.19, 5.1.37), numeral/dvigu luk (5.1.28) and the subordinate feminine affix also undergoing luk (1.2.49). It is precisely the source of obligatory tṛj-like behavior after this loss that is at issue.
two_derivations.circular_condition: Mahābhāṣya explicitly tests the mutual dependence if ṅīp both requires and triggers tṛj-like formation. It considers the gaṇa account, questions its membership, and then gives a route without a following overt trigger: the aṅga designation can follow from the elided affix. Its discussion of an aṅga designation differs from reactivating every aṅga operation under 1.1.63.
two_derivations.response_on_ngaish_side: Nyāsa offers the ca of 7.1.96 as including a case left unstated. In the comparison without lexical membership, the condition is semantic. The digital Nyāsa later records the spelling पञ्चक्रोष्टुभिरित्यत्र with u. Retain that local text while selecting the ṛ word directly common to the Bhāṣya and Kāśikā; the two texts are independently located.
two_derivations.accent: On the ṅīp route, tṛj supplies a final accented ṛ; the glide replacing it licenses the accent of the following feminine vowel under 6.1.174. Kāśikā specifies final udātta: kroṣṭrī́. This is a rule-backed accent for this reading, not an independent Vedic token.
two_derivations.additional_cases: Padamañjarī mentions the vocative, accusative plural, instrumental singular and dative singular while discussing the limits of rival accounts. Its current digital strings include malformed letter combinations. These examples are not turned into a complete counted paradigm.
